thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#23456 - prom_scrape_failures (service-metrics, us-east-1)
incident-bot: severity=high, alert_count=3 targets affected, runbook=https://redwood.runbooks/prom-scrape-failure

Mia (oncall): acked via PagerDuty :white_check_mark: I'm on it, pulling logs and checking exporter pods

Rajat: oncall - if it's the usual scrape timeout pattern, check exporter OOM/restart rates and node egress. Also check if scrape interval coord changed.

Mia (oncall): running quick checks:
```
kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app=node-exporter -o wide
kubectl -n monitoring logs deployment/metrics-scraper -c scraper --since=10m | tail -n 200
curl -s http://prom-us-east-1:9090/-/ready
```

Mia (oncall): node-exporter pods: 2/6 are CrashLoopBackOff on ip-10-0-4-12 and ip-10-0-4-15, restart count 4 in last 10m. metrics-scraper logs show repeated "context deadline exceeded" when scraping 10.0.4.12:9100

Alex: might be egress throttling or host-level CPU pressure. Any deploys to monitoring namespace in past hour?

Mia (oncall): checked deploys, nothing in past 3h. kubelet logs on ip-10-0-4-12 show high eviction pressure around 21:08 UTC.

Rajat: ok. Quick mitigation: 1) cordon and drain the two noisy nodes to let pods reschedule, 2) scale up the node-exporter DaemonSet to force placement on healthy nodes, 3) add a temporary scrape relabel to skip the problematic targets so Prom doesn't hang.

Mia (oncall): applying temporary relabel to skip problematic IPs now, linking the patch: https://git.redwood/ops/infra/patches/skip-bad-exporters (temp)

Priya: +1 to relabel. Also check log ingestion path - we've seen correlated log backlog when exporters OOM repeatedly. If logshipper is overloaded we'll get 5-10m ingestion delays reported by customer dashboards.

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: acknowledged by Mia (oncall) at 1728000525

Mia (oncall): cordoned ip-10-0-4-12 and ip-10-0-4-15, draining pods. Scaling node-exporter replicas to 4.

Alex: I'm watching Prometheus scrape failure rate: error rate dropped from 94% -> 40% after relabel, but still some timeouts when targets reschedule. Could be KV-store pressure on scrape targets.

Rajat: if reschedule is slow, we can fallback to the metrics-aggregator cache by redirecting scrape to fallback-cluster. Will coordinate with infra to flip route if needed.

Mia (oncall): customer impact check: Grafana alert for "metrics_latency_high" triggered for customer AcmeCorp dashboards (dashboard IDs: 3201, 3204) — metrics show missing series for 5m, some service SLIs are degraded but no 5xx spike reported to support yet. I notified Customer Ops.

Priya: good. Notify sales/account exec for AcmeCorp and include mitigation ETA. If SLA-facing metrics are impacted beyond 15m escalate to leadership.

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: escalated to Priya at 1728000850 (no ack from SRE lead within 15m)

Priya: jumping in. If drain doesn't stabilize within 10m, flip to fallback aggregate cluster. Also prepare a note for status page template: "Investigating partial metrics outages for subset of customers, no evidence of request/response failures to customers' services."

Mia (oncall): drain complete, pods rescheduled onto healthy nodes. node-exporter now 6/6 ready. Prometheus scrape error rate back down to 3% over last 2m.

Alex: logs show ingestion backlog peaked at ~18k events, current backlog draining at ~2k events/min. No data corruption.

Priya: thanks. Customer Ops, please post a brief incident message to AcmeCorp CS: explain partial metrics missing 08:20-08:30 UTC, data backfilled but dashboards may show gaps.

Mia (oncall): creating incident timeline in the runbook and setting PD to resolved pending postmortem:
- 1728000420 alert fired (prom_scrape_failures)
- 1728000450 Mia acked and started triage
- 1728000525 relabel applied to skip bad targets, drain nodes at 1728000600
- 1728000700 pods rescheduled, exporter's ready
- 1728000900 scrape error rate normalized, log backlog draining

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: PD#23456 status set to resolved by Mia at 1728002160 (manual close)

Mia (oncall): handing off to Priya for postmortem and customer comms. Priya, I left logs, commands, and runbook annotations in the incident doc.

Priya: taking the handoff. I'll draft a short postmortem and include recommended follow-ups: 1) node memory pressure alert tuning, 2) relabel safeguards for scrape timeouts, 3) add exporter readiness checks to avoid OOM loops.

Mia (oncall): thanks all :clap: closing thread after postmortem created.
